title: Day 6: Options Trading bot. up 36% today, up 11.3% YTD, 68% win rate
author: Lumpy-Owl-7795
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/4y2u8k901avh1.png?width=340&format=png&auto=webp&s=36ed96999345121ce6f815414976b7925c8d4ee5

From Day 1, people think I will blow up, but I haven't. Day 3, 4, and 5 had been losses and flat performance but that was my fault. Now I believe I should be consistent now. These are the changes I have made so far that took me from loss to now in profit

  
1. I removed the ability for the bot to manually close. I noticed this bot panics and sell just because of a minor -10% loss or a wick. Then the trade ended up going in profit or in the direction the bot actually planned. Right now, either I lose 30% or make 25, 50 and 100%. I do manually close the trade though. 

2. The bot is always optimizing the entry (never the exit). A good entry makes a good trade, so now, the entire prompt or skills are revolved around the bot optimizing the entry.

3. I noticed that the second trade results over a week have been very poor. The win rate of the first trade is 80%; second trade is 20%. So now, I updated the bot to pay close attention to second trade.   
  
 

https://preview.redd.it/clnt537c2avh1.png?width=1911&format=png&auto=webp&s=2ca3fa0d135633ee1a516522e990fbeb385789f8

I have 2 accounts, this $6300 is paper account. I still use this to gauge the performance over time. now this is at $6300, up about 15% since 10/17

**so if I had started trading real capital since September 18th,** I should be up almost 500% by now. let's see how I end the week...

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Posting the real account next to the paper one is the most useful part, since the $501 account is the one that shows what the fills are actually like. With 35 closed trades and a 24 to 11 record, the win rate has a wide margin (roughly plus or minus 15 points), so average win versus average loss and the worst day matter more, and a 0DTE book where one -30% loss cancels several +25% wins needs both numbers. Changing the rules after each bad stretch (removing the manual close, re-weighting the second trade) means the recent results are partly in-sample, so I’d freeze this version and score the next 50 trades separately. “Up almost 500% if I’d started with real capital” is a projection from paper fills, and paper options fills at the last price are optimistic. Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets, and 0DTE results often split sharply on CPI and FOMC days.

replies.author: Lumpy-Owl-7795
replies.body: I avoid FOMC. CPI is still great but once I see huge spike. I'll switch off the bot

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Avoiding FOMC is a sensible rule. For CPI, "switch it off once I see a spike" is a judgement made in the moment, so I'd write it down as a rule (for example a fixed size cut or pause window around the release, or a volatility threshold that turns the bot off automatically) and score those days separately, since a manual switch-off makes the results harder to compare across days.
